solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bad-tempered minister of religion outside house

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A grumpy vicar standing outside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The cleric's first letter stays outside on the left, the rest closes the house in on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric describes someone irritable and quick to anger, from the old humour of yellow bile.

clue.text: One wearing deerstalker maybe — one in country

indicators.note: whoever wears a garment is inside it, so the wearer sits within the clothing

blocks.note: a deerstalker is one kind of hat, hence 'maybe'
one as the Roman numeral I
one as the Roman numeral I again

explanation.surface: Someone in a Sherlock Holmes deerstalker, perhaps out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The first I goes inside HAT; the second simply follows. 'Country' is not rural land here but a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation sharing the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Inadequate character grabbing a daughter, a tearaway girl?

indicators.note: something inadequate falls short, so the word is left without its final letter
to grab is to take hold of, so one piece clutches the others inside it

blocks.note: a letter of the alphabet is a character
taken as written
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shady character snatching a young woman, who turns out to be a wild girl herself.
explanation.walkthrough: LETTER loses its last R to become LETTE, which then grabs A and D after its first letter. The question mark flags a slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is British slang for a young woman who drinks and behaves boisterously, like the stereotypical lads.

clue.text: Immature artist and wife

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the stock crossword artist
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A painter who has not grown up, and his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the artist crosswords reach for first.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw can mean inexperienced or untrained, as in a raw recruit, which is close to callow youth.

clue.text: Male or female’s argument against particular position

blocks.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
a stance is a position or attitude taken

explanation.surface: A debate where someone argues against a stated viewpoint, whatever their gender.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. The definition is a first name rather than a description of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a given name, now usually a woman's, but historically borne by men too.

clue.text: Irish tribe determined to seize power

indicators.note: seizing something means holding it tight, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: set on doing something means determined
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A clan of Irish rebels resolved to grab control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Determined' looks like part of the description of the tribe, but it is the outer word SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a branch or division of a family clan, especially in Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Composer was a model in England originally

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: a model sits for an artist, so she sat
the initial letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A musician who once worked as an artist's model in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was a model' means posed for a painter, which is sat, not walked a catwalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer famous for the Gymnopédies piano pieces.

clue.text: Go before and go back under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting under something places it lower, so it comes after in the answer

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to recede is to withdraw or move back

explanation.surface: Advancing and retreating while under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves use 'go': the first is the definition, the second, with 'back', means recede.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come or happen earlier than something else in time or order.

clue.text: One can see through this note penned by bereaved woman

indicators.note: something penned is shut in an enclosure, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a widow is a woman whose husband has died
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A grieving widow writing a letter that reveals everything about her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing a note, but it means enclosed, as in a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a glazed opening in a wall that lets people look out or in.

clue.text: Crazy individual’s name, say

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
to utter is to say aloud

explanation.surface: Someone mad giving their name, perhaps when introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutter is informal British slang for an eccentric or mentally unbalanced person.

clue.text: Second half of writer’s catalogue

indicators.note: taking only the latter half means the front part of the word is discarded

blocks.note: a novelist is a writer of fiction; ’s is the possessive 'of'

explanation.surface: The later pages of an author's book catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer has to be an eight-letter word whose back half is a word meaning catalogue: NOVELIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is an itemised record of names or things, which is what a catalogue is.

clue.text: Person protecting that place is troubled

indicators.note: protecting something means shielding it on all sides, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: bod is British slang for a person
there means in that place

explanation.surface: Someone guarding a spot is uneasy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bod is informal British for a person, short for body; 'that place' means there, not a named location.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered means worried or disturbed, the same sense as troubled by something.

clue.text: Famous runner one encountered on stairs?

blocks.note: first meaning: the athlete who first ran a mile in under four minutes, in 1954
second meaning: the handrail running up a staircase

explanation.walkthrough: A carpet strip on stairs is also called a runner, which tempts you towards carpets; Roger Bannister is the runner, and the stair rail can be spelt with two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Bannister was the record-breaking British miler, and a bannister is the rail people grip going up stairs.

clue.text: Untainted English in tribal group

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a clan is a group of families, a tribe
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A pure-blooded Englishman living among a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tribal group' is a four-letter group of families, and the English letter is placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means free from dirt, contamination or moral stain, just as untainted does.

clue.text: Satisfied with what’s inside

blocks.note: first meaning: pleased, happy with things, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: the material held within something, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Satisfied with what's inside' reads as one phrase about being pleased with contents; it is two meanings, joined by 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for being happy with one's lot and a noun for the material held inside a container.

clue.text: Bizarre runes one observed in hospital?

indicators.note: bizarre means strange and out of order, so the letters come in a strange new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strange ancient symbols spotted on a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is vague: many people are seen in hospital, but this one fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is a familiar sight on any hospital ward, caring for patients there.

clue.text: Hear pal upset painter

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Listen: a friend of yours has distressed an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like an instruction to listen, but it is just four letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was an Italian Renaissance master famed for his Madonnas and the School of Athens fresco.

clue.text: I mention going wrong very quickly

indicators.note: something going wrong is falling into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: I refer to things going badly, and it happens fast.
explanation.walkthrough: All eight letters of 'I mention' are rearranged into the three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means almost instantly, with hardly any delay at all.

clue.text: Arrangement to request food?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sequence or layout, as in alphabetical arrangement
second meaning: what diners do with a waiter in a restaurant

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a deal made to get a meal; the two halves are separate meanings joined by 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a sequence or system and a verb for asking a waiter to bring a dish.

clue.text: Classy shop refitted

indicators.note: a refit rebuilds the parts in a new layout, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An upmarket boutique after a refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classy shop' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the adjective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is informal for smart, elegant or upper-class, the same sense as classy.

clue.text: Birds together hide, conserving energy

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe within, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a hide is an animal's skin
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers sharing a hide, keeping still to save their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' suggests a birdwatching shelter, but it is the animal pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the collective noun for wild geese flying in formation.

clue.text: Grass — it gets to change again

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
taken as written

explanation.surface: An informer gets a chance to alter their story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' tempts as British slang for an informer; here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit is to revise text or film a second time, altering it once more.

clue.text: Faulty regulation adopted by US agent

indicators.note: what is adopted is taken in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: a fed is an American federal agent, such as an FBI officer
a law is a rule or regulation

explanation.surface: An American official taking on a defective rule.
explanation.walkthrough: FED is American slang for a federal agent, as of the FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawed means having defects or errors, which is what being faulty amounts to.

clue.text: Female, an ardent supporter

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who is a passionate follower.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'an' is wordplay, so the definition is just 'ardent supporter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiastic follower of a team, star or hobby.

clue.text: Celebrity, good person meeting a king

blocks.note: ST, a saint, is the stock crossword good person
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A famous, virtuous person being introduced to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for saint is the usual crossword good person, and R is from rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer or public figure, the same as a celebrity.

clue.text: Continuing to annoy Heather after row

indicators.note: coming after places one piece later in the reading order than the other

blocks.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone named Heather still irritating people after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name and 'row' like a quarrel; they are the plant and a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rankling causes lasting resentment or irritation, festering over time.
